OUTPUT 1: Livelihoods Opportunities Created in the Target Locations - 808 beneficiaries (301 women, 507 men; 495 youth) received on-the-job training - 89 beneficiaries received facilitation support for job placement (18 women, 71 men; 63 youth) - 978 (385 women, 593 men) beneficiaries in target locations received asset replacement grants - 462 (115 women, 347 men) existing business owners received cash grants to expand their business
OUTPUT 2: Entrepreneurship Promoted Among Beneficiaries - 1,291 start-ups (599 women, 692 men) received the grants for business start-ups - 1,504 beneficiaries (500 women, 1,004 men) trained in business management skills
OUTPUT 3: Opportunities for Local Employment Created in Target Locations - 11,770 workers (4,459 women, 7,311 men) employed in short-term cash-for-work schemes - 12,188 cash-for-work beneficiaries (4,547 women, 7,641 men) trained in vocational skills
OUTPUT 4: Enabling environment for MoLSA to support small enterprises and labour market improved - Operational plan for conducting the assessment is complete - Methodology for developing the SOPs manual on monitoring and following up with MoLSA-supported businesses is complete; - Areas of capacity building and training topics were identified. - Training plan is under development.

OUTPUT 2: Entrepreneurship Promoted Among Beneficiaries 2.1: 456 beneficiaries received grants for business start-ups (30% women) 2.2: 1435 beneficiaries received business management training 2.3: 90 % start-ups by beneficiary running successfully (30% women)
OUTPUT 3: Opportunities for Local Employment Created in Target Locations 3.1: 2182 workers employed in cash for work schemes (30% women) 3.2: 4961 CfW beneficiaries trained in vocational skills (30% women)
OUTPUT 4: Enabling environment for MoLSA to support small enterprises and labour market improved 4.1: Capacity assessment response is proposed 4.2: Minimum one SOPs manual developed 4.3: At least three capacity building and training programmes conducted.

OUTPUT 1: Livelihoods Opportunities Created in the Target Locations 1.1: 659 beneficiaries (303 women) received vocational training or OJT (46% women) 1.2: 743 trained beneficiaries (297 women, 432 youths) supported with job-placement in the private sector (40% women) 1.3: 678 beneficiaries (272 women) receive asset replacement grants (40% women) 1.4: 699 existing business owners (179 women) receive grants for SMEs (26% women)
OUTPUT 2: Entrepreneurship Promoted Among Beneficiaries 2.1: 1464 Beneficiaries (733 women) received grants for business start-ups (50% women) 2.2: 1464 beneficiaries (733 women) received business management training 2.3: 95.1 % (n=196) start-ups by beneficiary running successfully (48% women, n=99)
OUTPUT 3: Opportunities for Local Employment Created in Target Locations 3.1: 3461 workers (1189 women) employed in cash for work schemes (34% women) 3.2: 1797 CfW beneficiaries (837 women) trained in vocational skills (47% women)
OUTPUT 4: Enabling environment for MoLSA to support small enterprises and labour market improved 4.1: Two (2) institutional capacity assessment reports were prepared for MoLSA’s Business Incubators Section and Micro-Credit Fund Section.The institutional capacity assessment reports were reviewed and endorsed by MoLSA.
4.2: One SOPs manual on monitoring and following up with MoLSA-supported businesses was developed. The SOPs manual was reviewed and approved by MoLSA.
4.3: Seven (7) capacity building and training programmes were conducted.272 MoLSA employees (54 women) received capacity building training programmes. 23 MoLSA staff passed the accreditation test for being certified TOT on Preparing and Evaluating Feasibility Studies.
